body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「你個新模型在固定測試集高過 baseline 四個百分點。你會否即刻建議換走 baseline？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「會，因為分數高咗，模型一定更好。」

## 先講清楚比較的是甚麼

Baseline 不是一個用來襯托模型的低分對手，而是現時決定可以怎樣做的比較點。它可以是一條清楚規則、人工檢查表、既有排序，或者「先不自動化」的工作流。新模型高四分，仍然要問：是哪一個 metric？同一批固定 case 嗎？threshold 有沒有改？多出的正確答案會否剛好落在最容易的 case？錯的 case 會否令一位 reviewer 多花時間，或者把本來要停下來的項目送進錯誤 queue？

一個可用的比較應把 task contract 寫死：輸入是甚麼、輸出可作甚麼決定、誰會看結果、哪些 case 必須交回人。然後保留 baseline 的輸出，和候選模型逐項比較。若是 classification，可看 confusion matrix、threshold 前後的 error slice 和不確定 case；若是生成工作，可看固定 rubric、schema pass rate、引用是否可追溯，以及 reviewer 是否仍要重做。單一平均分是起點，不是結論。

## 熟路線是比較基準，不是陪襯

有人說新路線平均快四分鐘。出發前你仍會問：它會不會在下雨天塞車？會不會把你送到錯的出口？原本的路線雖然慢一點，是否較穩定、較容易解釋？Baseline 就是那條你已知代價的舊路，不是故意設得差來襯托新路。

## 答題時要交代嘅判斷

先把「模型較好」改成「在已定義的決定和風險下，候選方案是否比最低可接受做法少製造錯誤或重工」。如果新模型只改善離線分數，但令人工覆核量、延遲、成本或高風險錯誤變差，答案可以是保留 baseline。反過來，當規則型 baseline 已在模糊語句或多語輸入穩定失敗，新模型才有值得驗證的增量。

## 答案何時會太薄

不要一開始就比較十個模型或追 leaderboard。先做一個簡單、可重跑的 baseline：例如明確關鍵字規則加「不確定就交人」，或者一個固定表單。若這個 baseline 已滿足少量、低風險工作，先記錄它的失敗，再證明較複雜模型解決的是哪一種失敗。沒有決定、沒有固定 case 的模型比較，只是展示，不是 evaluation。

## 技術證據

可檢查的 artefact 包括 `problem-contract.md`、版本化的 `baseline.py` 或規則設定、`eval-cases.jsonl`、每個 case 的 expected decision、混淆矩陣、threshold sweep、錯誤 slice 表和一份固定輸出 diff。README 要寫明 random seed、資料切分、模型／prompt 設定和哪些 case 故意不自動處理。這些東西讓人看見四分從哪裡來，也讓人檢查它有沒有其實是資料或設定改了。

## 交付、業務與風險證據

另外寫一頁 `decision-record.md`：結果給誰看、只支援哪一個小決定、錯一次會造成甚麼重工、何時強制 human review，以及候選方案在哪個條件下不會替換 baseline。把「節省時間」留作待量度假設，不要將 synthetic evaluation 寫成真實成效。清楚的 stop condition 和 rollback 選項，往往比一個漂亮分數更能說明你知道交付的責任。

## 延伸閱讀

[把 model score 連回 workflow decision](/zh-HK/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)、[用證據而非流暢度評 Portfolio](/zh-HK/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency) 和 [由 offline evaluation 走到獲授權 pilot](/zh-HK/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。所有情境、數字、資料和 artefact 都是虛構教學草稿，用來練習比較方法；不描述任何真實機構、客戶、候選人、招聘程序或已達成的成果。

body.zh-Hans:
> 面试官问：“你的新模型在固定测试集比 baseline 高四个百分点。你会立刻建议换掉 baseline 吗？”
>
> 答对一半的答案：“会，因为分数变高，模型一定更好。”

## 先说清楚比较的是什么

Baseline 不是拿来衬托模型的低分对手，而是目前决策可以怎样做的比较点。它可以是一条明确规则、人工检查表、既有排序，或是“先不自动化”的工作流程。新模型高四分，仍要问：是哪一个 metric？是不是同一批固定 case？threshold 有没有改？增加的正确答案是否刚好都在容易案例？错误案例会不会让 reviewer 多花时间，或把原本该停下的项目送到错误 queue？

可用的比较要把 task contract 写清楚：输入是什么、输出可支持什么决策、谁看结果、哪些 case 必须交回人。接着保留 baseline 输出，与候选模型逐项比较。若是 classification，可以看 confusion matrix、threshold 前后的 error slice 和不确定案例；若是生成工作，则看固定 rubric、schema pass rate、引用是否可追溯，以及 reviewer 是否还要重做。单一平均分只是起点，不是结论。

## 熟悉路线是比较基准，不是陪衬

有人说新路线平均快四分钟。出发前你还是会问：下雨天会不会堵车？会不会把你送到错误出口？原本的路线虽然慢一点，是否更稳定、更容易解释？Baseline 就是那条你知道代价的旧路，不是故意设得很差来衬托新路。

## 面试真正想听到的判断

先把“模型比较好”改成“在定义好的决策与风险下，候选方案是否比最低可接受做法少制造错误或返工”。若新模型只提升离线分数，却让人工复核量、延迟、成本或高风险错误变差，答案可以是保留 baseline。反过来，当规则型 baseline 已在模糊语句或多语输入稳定失败，新模型才有值得验证的增量。

## 答案什么时候太薄

不要一开始就比较十个模型或追 leaderboard。先做一个简单、可重跑的 baseline：例如明确关键词规则加上“不确定就交人”，或一份固定表单。若 baseline 已满足少量、低风险工作，先记录它的失败，再证明较复杂模型解决的是哪种失败。没有决策、没有固定 case 的模型比较，只是展示，不是 evaluation。

## 技术证据

可检查的 artefact 包括 `problem-contract.md`、版本化的 `baseline.py` 或规则设置、`eval-cases.jsonl`、每个 case 的 expected decision、混淆矩阵、threshold sweep、错误 slice 表，以及固定输出的 diff。README 要写清楚 random seed、数据切分、模型／prompt 设置与哪些 case 刻意不自动处理。这些内容让人知道四分从哪里来，也可检查是否其实是数据或设置改了。

## 交付、业务与风险证据

另写一页 `decision-record.md`：结果给谁看、只支持哪个小决策、错一次会造成什么返工、何时强制 human review，以及候选方案在哪种条件下不会取代 baseline。把“节省时间”保留为待测量假设，不要把 synthetic evaluation 写成真实成效。清楚的 stop condition 与 rollback 选项，常比漂亮分数更能说明你理解交付责任。

## 延伸阅读

[把 model score 连回 workflow decision](/zh-Hans/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)、[用证据而非流畅度评 Portfolio](/zh-Hans/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency) 和 [从 offline evaluation 走到获授权 pilot](/zh-Hans/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 的单题练习。所有情境、数字、数据和 artefact 都是虚构教学草稿，用来练习比较方法；不描述任何真实机构、客户、候选人、招聘程序或已达成成果。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Your new model is four percentage points above the baseline on a fixed test set. Would you recommend replacing the baseline immediately?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Yes. The score is higher, so the model is better.”

## Name the thing being compared

A baseline is not a deliberately weak opponent that makes a model look impressive. It is the current, lowest-credible way to make a decision: a clear rule, a reviewer checklist, an existing ranking, or an intentional choice not to automate. A four-point gain still raises questions. Which metric moved? Were the cases and threshold frozen? Did the gain appear only on easy cases? Does a new error create extra review work or send a case that should stop into the wrong queue?

A useful comparison freezes a task contract: what enters, which decision the output may support, who reads it, and which cases must go back to a person. Preserve the baseline output and compare it case by case with the candidate. For classification, inspect the confusion matrix, error slices around the threshold, and uncertain cases. For generation, inspect a fixed rubric, schema pass rate, traceable citations, and whether a reviewer still has to redo the work. An average score starts the conversation; it does not finish it.

## A known route is a comparison, not a prop

Someone says a new route is four minutes faster on average. Before you take it, you still ask whether it stalls in rain, sends you to the wrong exit, or becomes impossible to explain when it fails. The old route may be slower but predictable. That known route is the baseline. It is not a bad route invented to flatter the new one.

## The judgement an interviewer is listening for

Replace “the model is better” with: “For a defined decision and risk boundary, does this candidate create fewer harmful mistakes or less rework than the minimum acceptable method?” If an offline score rises while review volume, latency, cost, or high-risk errors worsen, retaining the baseline can be the correct decision. The model earns a focused trial when the rule-based baseline repeatedly fails on a named class of ambiguity, such as mixed-language inputs, and the candidate can be tested against that failure.

## Where an answer goes thin

Do not begin by comparing ten models or chasing a leaderboard. Build a simple rerunnable baseline first: perhaps explicit keyword rules plus “hand uncertain cases to a person,” or a fixed form. If it is enough for a small, low-risk workflow, record its failures before claiming a more complex model solves one. A model comparison without a decision and fixed cases is a demonstration, not an evaluation.

## Technical evidence

An inspectable pack can include `problem-contract.md`, a versioned `baseline.py` or rule configuration, `eval-cases.jsonl`, an expected decision for each case, a confusion matrix, a threshold sweep, an error-slice table, and a fixed-output diff. The README should name the random seed, split, model or prompt configuration, and cases deliberately excluded from automation. These artefacts show where the four points came from and let a reviewer detect whether a data or setting change created the gain.

## Delivery, business, and risk evidence

Keep a separate `decision-record.md`: who sees the result, which small decision it supports, what rework one mistake can cause, when human review is mandatory, and when the candidate must not replace the baseline. Treat “time saved” as a hypothesis to measure, not a business outcome inferred from synthetic evaluation. A stop condition and rollback option often say more about delivery judgement than a polished score.

## Further reading

[Connect a model score to a workflow decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision), [score a portfolio by evidence rather than fluency](/en/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency), and [move from offline evaluation to an authorised pilot](/en/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Every scenario, number, dataset, and artefact is fictional teaching-draft material for practising a comparison method. It does not describe a real organisation, customer, candidate, hiring process, or achieved outcome.
